citations.assessment: Yose ben Shaul and Yochanan ben Shaul give distinct identifications of the item in the ruling.
Yochanan ben Shaul explains an exception involving a loaf from which challah or demai was removed. The attribution to Rabbi in the adjacent segment belongs to Yose ben Shaul.
Yochanan ben Shaul teaches the reason for bringing the heifer to an uncultivated valley.
Rabbi Levi explicitly cites Rabbi Yochanan ben Shaul regarding Joseph and Jacob’s blessing.
The pursued-person rule is attributed to Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul in the passage where Abaye discusses bloodshed.
The other Bavli locus also gives Yonatan ben Shaul in the discussion of stopping a pursuer by injuring a limb.
Heilprin’s reciprocal Yose entry explicitly lists Yochanan and Chalafta as brothers. The compared Bavli names Yose and Yochanan in one dispute without stating the kinship.

holds.reason: Preserve the Yuchasin attribution, student description and tentative error judgment. The parallel Heilprin entry is not a direct Yuchasin witness. The checked Bavli here gives Yochanan.
The two Heilprin notices agree on kinship. The exact Bavli passage verifies the two speakers, with kinship left open as a historical claim.
